7.1.simple: Krishna promises to show Arjuna how to know him fully and without doubt: by keeping the mind lovingly connected to him, practicing yoga and relying on him.

7.2.simple: Krishna will share both knowledge (understanding) and realization (living experience of it). Once this is truly known, nothing essential is left to learn.

7.3.simple: Out of thousands of people, few truly seek the highest, and among those, few come to know Krishna as he really is. Real understanding is rare and precious, so it is worth sincere effort.

7.4.simple: Krishna describes his material nature as eightfold: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and ego (the sense of 'I'). Even our thoughts belong to this changing nature.

7.5.simple: Beyond this lower, material nature is Krishna's higher nature: the living spirit, the conscious life in every being, which holds the whole world up.

7.6.simple: These two natures, matter and spirit, are the source from which all beings come. Krishna is the origin of the whole universe and the place it returns to.

7.7.simple: Nothing is higher than Krishna. Everything is held together by him, the way pearls are held together by a thread you cannot see.

7.8.simple: Krishna points to the divine in everyday things: the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon, the sacred sound Om, sound in space, and human strength.

7.9.simple: He is the sweet smell of the earth, the brightness of fire, the life in every living thing, and the discipline of those who practice self-control.

7.10.simple: Krishna is the timeless seed of all beings, the intelligence in the wise and the brilliance in everything that shines. Every gift points back to its source.

7.11.simple: He is strength that is free from greed and attachment, and desire that is in harmony with dharma (what is right). Not all wanting is bad; wanting what is right is sacred.

7.12.simple: All qualities of life, whether calm and pure (sattva), active and passionate (rajas), or dull and heavy (tamas), come from Krishna. They exist in him, but he is not limited by them.

7.13.simple: Caught up in these three moods of nature, people do not recognize Krishna, who is beyond them and never changes. We mistake the passing show for the whole truth.

7.14.simple: Maya (the divine power of illusion), woven from these three qualities, is hard to see through on our own. But those who turn to Krishna can cross beyond it.

7.15.simple: When illusion clouds a person's understanding, they may drift into harmful ways and stop seeking the divine at all. Krishna is describing how confusion blocks the path.

7.16.simple: Four kinds of good people turn to Krishna: those in distress, those curious to understand, those seeking something they need, and the wise. Every sincere reason is honored.

7.17.simple: Of these, the wise person, always steady and devoted to the One, stands out. Krishna is very dear to them, and they are very dear to him.

7.18.simple: All four are noble, Krishna says, but the wise one is like his very own Self, because their mind rests in him as the highest goal.

7.19.simple: After many lifetimes, the wise person realizes 'Vasudeva (the divine) is everything' and comes to Krishna. Such a great soul is very rare.

7.20.simple: When desires pull our wisdom away, we turn to lesser powers and rituals, shaped by our own nature, hoping to get what we want.

7.21.simple: Whatever form of the divine a person sincerely worships, Krishna himself makes their faith steady. Sincere faith of any kind is supported by him.

7.22.simple: Worshipping that form with faith, they receive what they hoped for, but it is really Krishna who grants it.

7.23.simple: When we seek only limited things, the rewards are limited and do not last. Those who worship lesser powers reach them; those devoted to Krishna reach Krishna.

7.24.simple: People who do not understand think of the unmanifest divine as merely a limited, visible form, missing Krishna's higher nature, which is unchanging and supreme.

7.25.simple: Krishna is hidden from many by his yoga-maya (his veiling power). The confused world does not recognize him as unborn and imperishable.

7.26.simple: Krishna knows every being of the past, present and future, yet no one fully knows him. The divine is always greater than our grasp.

7.27.simple: From birth, every being is confused by pairs of opposites born of liking and disliking. Our likes and dislikes quietly shape how we see everything.

7.28.simple: But those who live rightly, whose wrongdoing has come to an end and who are freed from the pull of opposites, worship Krishna with firm resolve.

7.29.simple: Those who take refuge in Krishna while seeking freedom from aging and death come to understand Brahman (the infinite reality), the true Self and the whole nature of action.

7.30.simple: Those who know Krishna as present in the material world, in the divine powers and in all sacrifice keep their minds steady and know him even at the time of death.

lessons.title: Look beneath the surface
lessons.teaching: Krishna offers knowledge that is lived, not just learned. Body, mind and even ego belong to the changing, outer layer of nature. Beneath it is a deeper, living spirit that holds everything up, and that is worth seeking sincerely.
lessons.keyIdea: You are more than your body, thoughts and image; life itself flows through you.

apply.scenario: Your posts get fewer likes than your friends', and lately your mood rises and falls with the numbers. You have started to feel worthless.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Post more often and copy trending styles until the numbers go up.
Remember that looks, opinions and image are only the surface, and nurture the deeper life within you.
Delete your accounts in anger and tell everyone social media is fake.
Compare your stats with your friends' every week to see where you stand.
apply.why: In 7.4-7.5 Krishna explains that body, mind and ego belong to his changing lower nature, while the deeper life that sustains everything is his higher nature.

lessons.reflect: What part of you stays the same no matter how others see you?
lessons.practice: Before checking your phone this morning, take one minute simply to notice that you are alive.

lessons.title: See the sacred in ordinary things
lessons.teaching: Everything is strung on the divine like pearls on a thread. Krishna points to himself in the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon, the fragrance of the earth, the life in living things and the intelligence of the wise. Ordinary moments can become reminders of something sacred.
lessons.keyIdea: The divine is the taste in water and the light in the sun.

apply.scenario: Your days feel gray and repetitive: commute, work, dinner, sleep. It seems life only really happens on holidays.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Plan your next holiday and simply endure the weeks until then.
Fill every spare moment with shows and scrolling to escape the boredom.
Accept that this flatness is just what adult life is like.
Pause in ordinary moments, like drinking water or feeling sunlight, and notice them as gifts from a deeper source.
apply.why: In 7.8 Krishna says he is the taste in water and the light of the sun and moon, so even everyday things can point to the sacred.

lessons.reflect: Where in an ordinary day have you felt a quiet sense of wonder?
lessons.practice: Drink one glass of water slowly today, really tasting it, with a moment of thanks.

lessons.title: Strength without greed
lessons.teaching: Krishna is the strength that is free from greed, and the desire that stays in harmony with what is right. All moods of nature, calm, restless or dull, come from him, but he is not caught in them. Illusion is hard to see through alone, yet turning toward the divine helps us cross it.
lessons.keyIdea: True strength is free of greed; good desire serves what is right.

apply.scenario: You are the strongest negotiator on your team. You could pressure a small supplier into an unfairly low price and earn yourself a bonus.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Use your skill to reach a fair deal that is good for both sides, even if your bonus is smaller.
Push the supplier as hard as you can; business is business.
Let your manager decide so it isn't your responsibility.
Take the low price this time and promise yourself you'll be fair next time.
apply.why: In 7.11 Krishna says he is the strength of the strong that is free from greed and attachment, and desire that does not go against dharma (what is right).

lessons.reflect: Which of your desires feel in harmony with what is right, and which pull against it?
lessons.practice: Use one of your strengths today to help someone, expecting nothing in return.

lessons.title: Every sincere seeker is welcome
lessons.teaching: People turn to the divine for different reasons: pain, curiosity, needs or wisdom. Krishna calls them all noble, while the wise who love him for his own sake are especially dear. When desires cloud our wisdom, we settle for smaller goals.
lessons.keyIdea: Whether you come in pain, curiosity or need, you are welcome.

apply.scenario: Your friend has started praying since her father fell ill. Another friend teases her for 'only turning to God when she's desperate'.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Agree with the teasing friend; faith that starts in a crisis isn't sincere.
Stay silent so you don't have to take sides.
Gently say that turning to the divine in hard times is real and honorable, and stand by her.
Tell her she should study religion properly before she starts praying.
apply.why: In 7.16-7.18 Krishna names the distressed among the four kinds of people who turn to him, and calls all of them noble.

lessons.reflect: What first drew you to questions of meaning or faith, and how has your reason changed over time?
lessons.practice: Write one honest sentence about what you are truly seeking in life right now.

lessons.title: Honor faith, seek what lasts
lessons.teaching: Krishna steadies anyone's sincere faith, whatever form they worship, and he is the one who grants its fruits. But rewards sought only for limited wishes do not last. The deepest reality is unborn and unchanging, greater than any single form we picture.
lessons.keyIdea: Sincere faith is always supported; seek what lasts, not only what passes.

apply.scenario: At a family gathering, relatives from different faith traditions start arguing about whose way of worship is the 'right' one.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Join in and defend your own tradition as the only real one.
Declare that all religion is pointless so the argument ends.
Leave the room and avoid these relatives in the future.
Respect each person's sincere faith, and gently steer the talk toward the deeper, lasting good each one seeks.
apply.why: In 7.21 Krishna says that whatever form a person worships with faith, he himself makes that faith steady, and 7.23 notes that limited aims bring limited fruits.

lessons.reflect: What do you hope your faith or values will bring you: something passing, or something lasting?
lessons.practice: Ask someone today what their faith or values mean to them, and simply listen.

lessons.title: Loosen your likes and dislikes
lessons.teaching: From birth we are pulled by opposites: liking and disliking, wanting and avoiding. Those who live well and loosen this pull find steady devotion. Taking refuge in the divine brings understanding of the true Self and a mind that stays steady, even at the very end.
lessons.keyIdea: Likes and dislikes color everything; loosen their grip and see clearly.

apply.scenario: A new teammate has a manner you disliked from day one, and you have noticed you dismiss every idea they suggest.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Notice your dislike, set it aside, and judge their ideas on their own merits.
Trust your gut; first impressions are usually right.
Avoid working with them so there is no conflict.
Pretend to agree with their ideas so you seem open-minded.
apply.why: In 7.27 Krishna says all beings are confused by the pairs of opposites born of desire and aversion, and in 7.28 the steady ones are those freed from that confusion.

lessons.reflect: Which of your strong dislikes might be shaping how you see someone unfairly?
lessons.practice: Catch one instant 'I don't like that' today and ask: is this true, or just habit?
